title: What happens to a gift card when a business closes?
sources: Federal Trade Commission Gift Card Rights

lines.text: If you have an unused fifty-dollar gift card to a retail store that files for bankruptcy, is your money gone?
lines.caps: What happens to your *gift card | when a store goes *bankrupt?

lines.text: The brutal legal reality is that gift card holders are considered unsecured creditors.
lines.caps: You become an *unsecured creditor | at the back of the *line!

lines.text: When a company files Chapter 11 bankruptcy, federal courts freeze operations to pay major lenders first.
lines.caps: Courts freeze assets to pay *banks | and bondholders *first

lines.text: The retailer must request special permission from the bankruptcy judge to continue accepting gift cards.
lines.caps: The judge decides *if | gift cards will still be *honored

lines.text: If the company shifts to total liquidation, gift card redemptions are terminated instantly.
lines.caps: In liquidation, cards become *worthless | pieces of plastic *instantly!

lines.text: You can file a formal claim with the bankruptcy court, but cardholders typically receive only pennies on the dollar years later.
lines.caps: Court claims pay only *pennies | on the dollar years *later

lines.text: Always spend gift cards as soon as you receive them rather than stashing them in a drawer.
lines.caps: Spend your gift *cards fast | before they expire or *vanish!
